question:
(i) State Ampere’s circuital law. Using it, obtain the expression for the magnetic field inside an ideal toroid having $N$ turns and carrying current $I$.
(ii) A toroid has $750$ turns and carries a current of $2.4\text{ A}$. Calculate the magnetic field at a point inside the toroid at radius $0.12\text{ m}$. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}$.

options.A: Ampere’s law gives $B(2\pi r)=\mu_0I$, so $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}$. For the toroid, $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}=4.0\times10^{-6}\,\text{T}$.
options.B: Ampere’s law is $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l=\mu_0I_{\text{enclosed}}$. For a circular path inside a toroid, $B(2\pi r)=\mu_0NI$, hence $B=\dfrac{\mu_0NI}{2\pi r}$. Thus, $B=\dfrac{(4\pi\times10^{-7})(750)(2.4)}{2\pi(0.12)}=3.0\times10^{-3}\,\text{T}$.
